messages:
jamie: throwing an idea out there — instead of client-side per-widget RBAC, what if the query layer does a single authz pass for the whole dashboard (batch keys)? fewer RPCs from browser and consistent enforcement.

nina: sounds good in theory. dashboards can produce lots of keys though. how do you bound it?

jamie: dedupe keys, cap batch (eg 200), prioritize visible widgets. overflow -> coarse tenant-level check or mark widgets 'authz_pending'.

mark: main ops risk = tail latency and stale policies. we need an in-process L1 policy cache LRU + watch invalidations. define cache_window_ms (default 500ms) so tenants can trade correctness vs perf.

leila: UX/security: default deny on ambiguity. offer explicit permissive_fallback only for aggregate-only dashboards. optimistic paths must be opt-in.

nina: metrics to collect: batch_size, batch_miss_rate, batch_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), authz_fallback_rate. SLO targets: batch p95 < 30ms, p99 < 200ms.

jamie: rollout plan: feature-flag in Console+Query, internal staging canary, 5% user traffic smoke, then ramp. add routing-level kill-switch and leak-detection job comparing old vs new decisions.

ops-bot: scheduled canary job authz-batch-smoke at 1761112400 — will post results.

mark: actions: prototype L1 cache and multiget flow (mark, due EOW); leila: sharding + eviction sketch (due Tue); nina: rollout checklist and metrics (due Wed); jamie: RFC draft with guarantee matrix (due Fri).

jamie: will add trace tags (authz.batch_id, authz.policy_id) and audit events for denies. thanks :thumbsup:
